sentences.text:
State Vs. Om Prakash & Ors
 Fir No. 138/2004
 Ps: Prashad Nagar

Date of Institution of case : 24.12.2007
Date of Judgment reserved : 25.10.2025
Date on which judgment pronounced : 07.11.2025
 Judgment
1. Cr. Case No. : 290492/2016 2. Date of commission of offence: 16.09.1998 3. Name of complainant: SMT. GEETA DEVI

4. Name and address of accused : (1) OM PRAKASH S/o Sh. Tulsi Ram, (expired on 09.06.2018) (2)
KASTURI LAL S/o Sh. Tulsi Ram, (expired on 08.03.2023) (3) JUGAL KISHORE S/o Sh. Tulsi Ram, R/o 11835/7, Sat Nagar, Karol Bagh, Delhi.
PS Prashad Nagar (4) CHANDER SAIN S/o Sh. Tulsi Ram, (expired on 13.01.2022) (5) GULAB CHAND S/o Sh. Tulsi Ram, (expired on 03.01.2011) (6) MADAN LAL S/o Sh. Tulsi Ram, (expired on 16.11.2016)
5. Offence complained of : U/s 420/468/471/34 IPC or proved 6.
Plea of accused : Pleaded not guilty 7.
Final Order : ACQUITTED 1.
Property generally creates rift and more particularly between siblings despite the fact that everyone knows that none has ever taken any property to the other world.

When a person dies,
he/she before death either divides the property amongst the descendants mostly through testament or leave the property at the whims of legal heirs.
He opts for the first option with a hope that after his death, the siblings will not fight with each other.
Unfortunately, the present timeline is such that even the wishes of dead are not respected.
Irrespective of whether the deceased has left behind a Will or has left the property untouched, siblings generally start fighting after sometime.

Normally,
State vs Om Prakash on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75317743/
1 such property disputes are fought before civil forums.
However, depending PS Prashad Nagar upon the price escalation of the property or the adventurous nature of the person, the dispute is given criminal color in one way or the other.
2. Present case is an example of fight between siblings in respect of a property left behind by their mother.
One Mathura Devi apparently inherited the property no.101 from her father who was allotted with the same by the government.
She had 6 sons and 2 daughters.
She died in the year 1978.
All the sons claimed that Mathura Devi had left a Will giving the property to them in exclusion of the daughters.
They therefore applied to the government for substitution of their names in the record on the basis of the Will.
They also given an affidavit of one daughter showing no objection to their proposal.
Government acted on such proposal and substituted the names of sons.
Later, they obtained a free-hold right in the property in usual course.
We are not concerned with the free-hold right in the present case.
We are just considering the circumstances related to the substitution of name.
3. The daughter whose affidavit was so given to the government became aware about such process after sometime.
She obtained a copy of affidavit from the government department.
She looked at the affidavit and was shocked to note her signature.
She did not sign such affidavit.
It is then that she entertained a thought that her brothers have played fraud on her and also on the government department for substituting their names in the record on the basis of false document.
She was also of the opinion that the Will of Mathura Devi as presented was not PS Prashad Nagar a genuine Will as her mother never executed such Will.
4. Aggrieved and shocked with the fraudulent conduct, she approached the police with a complaint but of no avail.
She thought of coming to the court and here, she found some solace.

A Ld.
Magistrate considered her grievance and opined that the matter needed a thorough investigation and accordingly he directed the police.
In turn, the police registered an FIR and investigated the matter.
5. In the name of investigation, the police simply obtained the handwriting of the daughter and sons and sent the same for forensic examination which opined that daughter did not sign the document.

Police arrested the sons and presented a chargesheet for offences punishable under Section-420,
468, 471, 34 IPC.
6.
When the time came, charge was framed against 5 brothers as one had already died.
Since there was a plea of not guilty, the prosecution was allowed to lead its evidence.

Prosecution examined several witnesses such as PW1/HC Devender, PW2/Geeta Devi, PW3/ HC Jaswant,
PW4/Bibkananda Pal, PW5/HC Yograj, PW6/Inspector Ranjan Kumar Singh, PW7/SI Sohal Lal,
PW8/Inspector Ajay Karan Sharma, PW9/Inspector Surya Prakash, PW10/Hari Kishan Beniwal and PW11/Narender Singh.
During the course of proceedings, 4 more brothers died and only one remained.
Statement of accused Jugal Kishore (the only alive accused) was recorded for the purpose of Section-313 CrPC.
Accused did not lead any evidence and even failed to advance arguments.
Matter was then reserved for judgment PS Prashad Nagar leaving the accused to file written submissions, however, he did not file the same.
Present judgment will dispose of the case.

State vs Om Prakash on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75317743/
2

Base of the case:
7.
Case of the prosecution is simply that the accused persons filed an affidavit of Geeta before the government department whereas Geeta never signed the said affidavit.
As such, the accused persons committed forgery and cheating.
The claim is almost entirely based on the forensic report showing that the affidavit was not signed by Geeta.
Reliability of forensic report:
8. IO suo moto took handwriting sample of Geeta and sent the same for forensic examination.
The signature of Geeta is in Hindi requiring just two consonants.
It is not hard to write the same with slight distinction.
9. We need to bear in mind that Geeta was raising allegations against her brothers and claiming that she had not signed the affidavit.
It does not require a Solomon's wisdom to understand that if the signature matches, there won't be any case at all.

Therefore, it cannot be ruled out that with a view to make a result certain, Geeta simply tweaked her writing style and wrote the sample before the IO in a different manner than that appearing on the affidavit.
10. The inference gets further strength from the fact that signature of Geeta is appearing differently at different places.
Her examination in chief and cross examination has been recorded in PS Prashad Nagar this case.
She signed in English.
Almost on every page, her signature appears with slight deviation.
If her signatures (made in one go) can appear differently, it cannot be ruled out that her signatures made with the gap of several years can also appear differently.
11. Geeta got married in the year 1978.
She is 7 th class pass.
It is highly unlikely that she used to put her signature in English.

Despite the same, it seems that signature of Geeta is appearing in English in the documents available in court file but interestingly no contemporary document has been filed to show that earlier also she used to sign in English.
She had lodged a complaint with the police in respect of the present allegations and signed the same in English.
She has deposed in this case and signed the same in English.
This indicates a deliberate attempt to sign in English.
However, even the signature done in English at different places are at variance.
Such difference in signature done at different places by Geeta shows that the signature in English has been done with efforts.
There is no consistency which generally comes to a person who usually puts his signature in English.

It can safely be inferred that Geeta was trying hard not to put her signature in Hindi in any document which could be used in court or in any document which is required to be signed in court such as the testimony.
12. Be that as it may, this court is of the opinion that the IO committed mistake in taking the handwriting sample of Geeta and basing it for comparison.

It would have been more prudent had the IO obtained contemporary documents having signature of PS Prashad Nagar Geeta and then made the same as base for comparison with the signature on the affidavit.
It would not have given any chance to Geeta to tweak her signature with a view to show variance.

Such contemporary documents would have shown as to whether Geeta was usually putting her signature in Hindi or in State vs Om Prakash on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75317743/
3 English.
Such contemporary documents further would have shown the writing style of Geeta without any chance of manipulation.
The IO however did not do so.
There is nothing on record to show that IO ever tried to collect any contemporary document of Geeta.

13. In the available circumstances, this court is of the opinion that a forensic result given on the basis of a sample signature taken by the IO (instead of a contemporary document), should not be given much credit.
This is apart from the fact that in terms of Section-45 of the Evidence Act, an expert report is just an opinion and does not bind the court.
Circumstances do not inspire confidence that Geeta did not sign the affidavit.
The expert report is liable to be and is discarded.

Veracity of affidavit:
14.
There is one additional reason to doubt the prosecution claim.
Affidavit of Geeta is dated 08.09.1998.
This affidavit was not sworn before any ordinary person.
It seems to be attested by a 1st class executive magistrate.
There is no claim of the complainant or the police or the prosecution that the said executive magistrate did not attest the affidavit.
Official act has to be treated as done in proper manner and an act of 1 st class executive magistrate cannot be doubted on the mere asking of the PS Prashad Nagar complainant.
Even if police wanted to claim a forgery, the said executive magistrate would have been the best person to show as to whether he attested the affidavit in the absence or presence of Geeta.
If an official act is done by an executive magistrate, it shall be treated as properly done, meaning that it was done in the presence of Geeta, unless of course a contrary scenario is shown to exist.
Prosecution has not shown that the executive magistrate did not attest the affidavit.
Therefore, this court is not inclined to accept that the affidavit was a forged one.

Complicity of accused persons:
15. Once the expert report goes, no material will remain which can implicate the accused persons in any manner.
Claim of Geeta that she had not signed the affidavit is doubtful.
No one had seen any accused signing the affidavit.
Even the expert has not said that any of the accused persons had signed the affidavit.
Prosecution however would like to claim that accused is the ultimate beneficiary and therefore, he should be treated as culprit for forging the affidavit of complainant.
This court is of the opinion that the claim cannot be accepted.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sheila Sebastian vs R.
Jawahar AIR 2018 SC 2434 has declined to follow the concept that a person who will have the benefit will be an accused simply on that count.

entities.text:
Sheila Sebastian vs R.
Jawahar AIR 2018 SC 2434
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Even if the affidavit was to be treated as forged,
prosecution ought to have establish that any of the accused persons was maker of the forged document.
Prosecution has miserably failed in this respect.
No cheating against the complainant:
16. Geeta has initiated the instant case.
She however cannot PS Prashad Nagar claim to have been cheated at all.
A Will of Mathura Devi is in existence.
It is not sufficient for Geeta to claim that her mother Mathura Devi had never executed any such Will.
Reason is obvious.

She cannot claim to know every activity of her mother. Section-213 of Indian Succession Act is not applicable to Delhi and therefore, there is no mandate that a Will should be probated before a person can receive State vs Om Prakash on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75317743/
4 benefit.
Meaning thereby that once a Will comes into existence and the testator dies, the beneficiary will be entitled to enjoy the benefit.
Clearly, after the death of Mathura Devi, the sons were entitled to claim themselves as owner of the property by virtue of the Will.
If Geeta wanted to dispute the Will, she was required to file a civil suit for declaration against the Will.
But she cannot be allowed to assume herself the role of a judge and declare that the Will is forged.
Until such a declaration is given by a competent court, the Will shall remain valid and shall confer proper title on the beneficiary.
In such circumstances, Geeta cannot claim any right over the property at all.

17. There is no claim of Geeta that any of the brothers induced or deceived her or made her part with the money or do a thing which she would not have done otherwise. Section-420 IPC can be invoked only when the necessary ingredients of cheating defined under Section-415 IPC are satisfied.
In the instant case, Geeta was never deceived or induced.
Therefore, she cannot claim to be cheated.

18. At best, Geeta could have claimed that accused persons had cheated the government by presenting a false affidavit as in PS Prashad Nagar the absence thereof, the government would not have substituted their names in the record.
In that scenario, a case for cheating might be made out (this comment is on the assumption that the affidavit might have been proved to be forged).
However, it is not for Geeta to take on herself the job of the government department.
It was for the government department to lodge a case if it was so aggrieved.
Prosecution does not claim that government department has come forward to lodge a case of cheating.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mohd. Ibrahim vs State of Bihar 2010 AIR SCW 405, has declined to accept a cheating case filed by an owner of the property which was sold by one person to another person.

entities.text: Mohd. Ibrahim vs State of Bihar 2010 AIR SCW 405
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was opined therein that owner was not cheated and it was only the said third person who could have filed a case of cheating.
Similar would be the position here and therefore, at the instance of Geeta, a case of cheating cannot be made out.

Result:
19.
In the result of the aforesaid analysis, it is held that case projected by the prosecution does have sufficient loopholes.

Prosecution has clearly not been able to establish the case and therefore, the accused who is alive i.e. JUGAL KISHORE is acquitted and the accused who are in other world, shall be deemed to be acquitted, from the from the charge of the present case.
